4.1.2.platform: Bootstrap / hand-rolled accordion using <a> or <div> headers
4.1.2.name: Accordion header is a non-button with no expanded state
4.1.2.description: Developers copy the accordion visual (a clickable bar that opens a panel) but build the trigger as <a href="#"> or a <div onclick>. The element exposes no button role, no aria-expanded, and aria-controls never points at the panel, so a screen reader user cannot tell the control is a toggle, cannot tell whether the section is open or closed, and may hear it as a link that goes nowhere.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Shipping & Returns
...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Partially detectable: axe flags interactive controls without discernible state only in some configs, but a bare <a href="#"> with visible text passes name/role checks because it IS a valid link with a name. The defect is that the role is wrong (link, not button) and the missing aria-expanded is on an element axe does not know is supposed to be a disclosure, so the toggle-state rule never fires.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: 216digital and BarrierBreak both name 'removing role=button from accordion headers' and 'aria-expanded value not changing on interaction' as the top recurring accordion defects. https://216digital.com/accordion-accessibility-common-issues-fixes/ and https://www.barrierbreak.com/top-5-aria-implementation-errors/

4.1.2.platform: Custom <div>/<span> 'button' (icon buttons in CMS widgets, hamburger toggles)
4.1.2.name: Visible label mismatches accessible name on a div-button
4.1.2.description: A control rendered as <div class="btn"> shows the word 'Menu' or a gear icon visually, but its accessible name comes from a stale aria-label like 'button' or 'toggle-1', or from an icon-font ligature that reads as gibberish. The visible text and the computed accessible name disagree, so voice-control users who say 'click Menu' fail, and screen reader users hear the wrong label.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Menu
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe sees a role=button WITH a non-empty accessible name (aria-label="toggle-1") and a tabindex, so it passes 'buttons must have discernible text' and 'aria roles used must conform.' Detecting that 'toggle-1' is not the visible 'Menu' requires reading the rendered glyph/text and comparing it semantically to the computed name — a visual+linguistic judgment no DOM linter makes reliably.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Harvard HUIT and the freeCodeCamp custom-dropdown guide both document that custom controls whose visible label does not match the accessible name break voice control and confuse screen reader users. https://accessibility.huit.harvard.edu/provide-name-role-and-value-information

4.1.2.platform: Modal dialog (jQuery UI dialog, hand-rolled overlay, many CMS lightboxes)
4.1.2.name: Fake modal: aria-modal set but background not inert and focus not trapped
4.1.2.description: The overlay div carries role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and looks modal, but the developer never traps Tab, never moves initial focus into the dialog, and leaves the background page focusable. Keyboard users Tab straight out of the dialog and onto hidden page content behind the scrim; screen reader users may also reach background content because aria-modal alone does not make content inert.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static analysis sees correct ARIA: role=dialog + aria-modal=true + accessible name all pass. Whether focus is actually trapped, whether initial focus moves into the dialog, and whether the background is truly inert are runtime keyboard behaviors that require operating the page with Tab/Shift+Tab — axe/WAVE/Lighthouse never press keys.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: MDN and TPGi stress that aria-modal="true" 'does not actually make the element modal — the developer must implement the modal behaviour'; TPGi's modal-accessibility survey found focus management as the most common real failure. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-modal and https://www.tpgi.com/the-current-state-of-modal-dialog-accessibility/

4.1.2.platform: Tabs widget (Bootstrap nav-tabs, hand-rolled tab UIs)
4.1.2.name: Tabs with no roving tabindex / no arrow-key support
4.1.2.description: Tab strips use role="tablist"/role="tab" markup (or just styled links) but every tab is a separate Tab stop and arrow keys do nothing. Users must Tab through all tabs, and roving tabindex (one tabindex=0, rest -1) is absent, breaking the APG keyboard contract. Often aria-selected is also static or missing.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
• Overview
  • Specs
  • Reviews
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe has a 'tablist must contain tabs' structural check but does not verify the roving-tabindex pattern or arrow-key handling — those are runtime keyboard behaviors. A page where every tab is independently Tab-focusable is technically operable, so it does not fail any static rule; the broken expectation (arrow keys move between tabs) is only observable by operating it.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: MDN tab/tablist role docs and Deque's A11y Support Series both specify roving tabindex (active tab tabindex=0, others -1) and arrow-key navigation as the contract that custom tabs routinely omit. https://www.deque.com/blog/a11y-support-series-part-1-aria-tab-panel-accessibility/

4.1.2.platform: Combobox / autocomplete (typeahead search, React-Select clones, hand-rolled)
4.1.2.name: Autocomplete results not announced; missing aria-expanded/activedescendant
4.1.2.description: A search input shows a dropdown of suggestions visually, but the input lacks role="combobox", aria-expanded never flips to true when the list opens, and aria-activedescendant is not set as the user arrows through results. Screen reader users get no announcement that suggestions appeared, how many there are, or which one is highlighted.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
• apple
  • apricot
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The input is a valid text field and the list is a valid <ul> — both pass static checks individually. The relationship (input controls a popup list whose active option must be announced) and the missing live/activedescendant feedback only manifest while typing and arrowing, so DOM-snapshot tools cannot see the broken announcement loop.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: The a11ysupport.io APG combobox test and Pope Tech's combobox guide document that aria-expanded must toggle and aria-activedescendant must track the highlighted option, and that omitting them is the dominant real-world combobox failure. https://a11ysupport.io/tests/apg__aria-1-2-combobox-with-list-autocomplete-example

4.1.2.platform: Custom toggle switch (settings switches in dashboards, theme togglers)
4.1.2.name: Switch with no role/state and on/off shown by color/position only
4.1.2.description: A pill-shaped toggle is built from two divs; the 'on/off' state is conveyed only by knob position and color. There is no role="switch", no aria-checked, and frequently no accessible name (the visible label is a separate, unassociated div). Screen reader users hear nothing useful and cannot tell if the setting is on or off.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Email notifications
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: If the switch has no role and no name, axe may flag a focusable element with no accessible name in some cases — but many of these get an aria-label and STILL fail because aria-checked is missing or never updates. Detecting that on/off is conveyed by knob position + color alone (use-of-color failure) and that the state is unannounced requires visual interpretation of the rendered control, not markup parsing.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Accessibility Insights 'aria-toggle-field-name', the A11Y Collective, and Atomic A11y checklist all flag missing role=switch / aria-checked / accessible name as the recurring custom-switch defect. https://accessibilityinsights.io/info-examples/web/aria-toggle-field-name/

4.1.2.platform: Menu button + role=menu (app 'kebab' menus, navigation 'mega menus')
4.1.2.name: role=menu misused for site nav; no arrow keys, no haspopup, links not menuitems
4.1.2.description: Developers slap role="menu"/role="menuitem" onto a navigation dropdown of links, or onto an actions menu, but never implement the APG menu keyboard model: no aria-haspopup on the trigger, no focus moved to the first item on open, arrow keys do nothing, Escape does not close. 4.1.2.platform: Tooltip (title-attribute tooltips, CSS :hover tooltips, icon-info tooltips)
4.1.2.name: Tooltip not dismissible/hoverable/persistent and tied only to hover
4.1.2.description: Help text appears on mouse hover (often via the native title attribute or a CSS :hover-only popup). It disappears the instant the pointer moves, cannot be dismissed with Escape, cannot be hovered to read, and never appears on keyboard focus. Low-vision users who magnify and need to move the pointer onto the tip lose it; keyboard users never see it.

4.1.2.platform: Custom slider (price range filters, noUiSlider clones, hand-rolled drag handles)
4.1.2.name: Slider with no role/value and no keyboard operation
4.1.2.description: A draggable thumb on a track is built from divs with a mousedown handler. There is no role="slider", no aria-valuenow/min/max, no aria-valuetext, and arrow keys do nothing. The intent ('this draggable thing is a value control') requires visually recognizing the slider, which a linter cannot do.

4.1.2.platform: Carousel / slider (Slick, Swiper defaults, hero banners on CMS themes)
4.1.2.name: Auto-rotating carousel with no pause control and no slide announcement
4.1.2.description: A hero carousel auto-advances every few seconds with no visible/operable pause-stop-hide control. Slides change under keyboard focus, focus is lost when the focused slide rotates away, off-screen slides remain in the tab order and accessibility tree, and slide changes are not exposed via group/aria-roledescription/live region. Big Sale
New In

4.1.2.platform: Disclosure / 'Show more' / 'Read more' (CMS content blocks, FAQ widgets)
4.1.2.name: Disclosure trigger with generic name and no expanded state
4.1.2.description: A 'Read more' / 'Show more' control expands hidden text but is a link or div with no aria-expanded and no aria-controls, and its accessible name is just the repeated generic phrase. Screen reader users get a list of identical 'Read more' controls with no context of what each reveals and no indication of open/closed state.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Read more
Full product description...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe can flag missing discernible text but cannot flag a NON-descriptive name that is technically present ('Read more' is a valid accessible name). Judging that 'Read more' is ambiguous out of context (2.4.4) and that the missing aria-expanded matters because this is a disclosure both require human semantic interpretation of purpose; the toggle role itself is not declared so no state rule fires.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: The APG disclosure pattern requires aria-expanded on the trigger; WebAIM and link-purpose guidance repeatedly cite generic repeated 'Read more'/'Learn more' from CMS widgets as a classic 2.4.4 ambiguous-link-text failure. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/

4.1.2.platform: alertdialog (confirm/destructive dialogs, 'Are you sure?' modals)
4.1.2.name: Critical confirm dialog uses role=dialog (or none) so it is not announced
4.1.2.description: A 'Delete account — are you sure?' modal is built with role="dialog" (or plain divs) rather than role="alertdialog", and focus is not moved into it. The urgent message is not announced as an alert, focus stays behind it, and a screen reader user may confirm a destructive action without ever hearing the warning.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Delete your account? This cannot be undone.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=dialog is valid ARIA, so no rule fails. Whether the dialog SHOULD be an alertdialog (because it carries an urgent, action-blocking message) is a semantic/contextual judgment about the content's importance; whether focus moves into it and the alert is announced are runtime behaviors. No static linter weighs the urgency of a message.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: APG distinguishes alertdialog (interrupts with an important message requiring a response) from dialog; MDN dialog-role docs note focus must move into the dialog — both are commonly skipped on confirm/destructive modals. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/dialog_role

4.1.2.platform: Listbox (custom <select> replacements, country/option pickers)
4.1.2.name: Custom listbox: options not announced, selection state visual-only
4.1.2.description: A fake select shows a styled options panel of <li> items. The trigger lacks combobox/button semantics with aria-expanded, the panel is not role="listbox" with role="option" children, selection is shown only by a checkmark/highlight (no aria-selected), and focus/active option is not tracked. Screen reader users cannot tell which option is selected or how many exist; keyboard arrow navigation through options is often missing.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
United States
  • United States
  • Canada
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The trigger div has an accessible name and the list is a valid <ul>, so static checks pass. That selection is conveyed only by a CSS class/checkmark (no aria-selected — a use-of-color/visual-only-state issue) and that arrow-key navigation is absent are visual and runtime judgments. The freeCodeCamp and Chris Henrick writeups stress native <select> is far safer precisely because these get botched.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: freeCodeCamp's accessible custom-dropdown guide and Chris Henrick's 'Custom and Accessible Select Menus Aren't Easy' document missing role=listbox/option, missing aria-selected, and absent keyboard support as the standard custom-listbox failures. https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-build-an-accessible-custom-dropdown-select-element/

4.1.2.platform: Spinbutton / number stepper (quantity +/- controls in carts)
4.1.2.name: Stepper +/- buttons with icon-only names and no spinbutton value semantics
4.1.2.description: A quantity stepper has '+' and '−' buttons (often unlabeled icon glyphs) around a value, but the value display is a plain <span> with no role="spinbutton"/aria-valuenow, and the increment/decrement buttons have no accessible name (just a glyph) or a name that does not say what they change. Screen reader users hear 'button button' and an unchanging value when they press them.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: 1
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: If the buttons contain a glyph character (−/+) axe may consider them to have text and pass discernible-text; the '−' may even be read as 'minus' or skipped. Judging that the name does not convey 'decrease quantity' is semantic, and the value <span> not exposing changes (no spinbutton role / live update) is a runtime announcement gap a snapshot scan cannot detect.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: The APG spinbutton pattern requires role=spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max and accessible names on the controls; e-commerce quantity steppers commonly ship as glyph-only buttons around a non-semantic value span, a frequent audit finding. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/

4.1.2.platform: WebAIM Million corpus (all builders) — buttons styled as div/span, icon-only controls
4.1.2.name: Empty button / icon control with no accessible name
4.1.2.description: A control is rendered as <div>, <span>, <a>, or an icon font/SVG with no text node and no aria-label, so its accessible name is empty. Screen readers announce 'button' or 'link' with nothing else. Common with hamburger menus, cart/search icons, social-share icons, and 'X' close buttons in page-builder widgets.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably caught by axe/WAVE ('button-name', 'link-name', 'Empty Button', 'Empty Link') — it is a pure programmatic check for an empty accessible name. Included for completeness as a high-prevalence baseline. Flagged humanJudgmentNeeded=false.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million 2026: empty buttons on 30.6% of home pages, empty links on 46.3% — both in the top six errors: https://webaim.org/projects/million/

4.1.2.platform: Shopify product pages, WooCommerce variation swatches, custom theme color/size pickers
4.1.2.name: Color-only variant swatches with no text label
4.1.2.description: Product variants are presented as colored squares/circles with no visible or programmatic text. The accessible name is empty or just a hex/SKU, and the selected state is shown only by a border or color change. Screen-reader and colorblind users cannot tell which color is which, nor which is currently selected.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: An empty-name swatch built as a div may trip a name check, but the deeper failures — that COLOR is the only means of conveying the option (1.4.1) and that the SELECTED state is communicated by visual styling alone — require a human to perceive the colors and reason that meaning is lost without them. No linter knows 'navy vs maroon' is the information.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Shopify's own accessibility best-practices doc warns custom swatches commonly lose keyboard access and text labels: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/accessibility . EAA-driven swatch fixes: https://craftshift.com/shopify-european-accessibility-act-swatches/

4.1.2.platform: accessiBe / UserWay / AudioEye overlay widgets injected over any CMS
4.1.2.name: Overlay-injected accessible names that mismatch the visible control
4.1.2.description: An automated accessibility-overlay 'fixes' controls by injecting aria-labels guessed from nearby text, icons, or filenames. The injected name frequently does not match the control's visible label or function (a 'Search' field labeled 'button', a close 'X' labeled 'menu'), so the accessible name and visible label diverge — and the widget can also trap screen-reader focus after its own dialog closes.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<!-- overlay rewrites this -->
<button aria-label="link 2">Contact Us</button>
<input type="search" aria-label="submit" placeholder="Search...">
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Both the overlay's injected name and the visible label are syntactically valid, so a linter sees an accessible name present and passes. Detecting that the programmatic NAME contradicts the VISIBLE label (and that voice-control users can no longer say the label) requires comparing rendered text against the computed name — a human semantic comparison. Tools that scan post-overlay DOM are actively fooled.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: FTC fined accessiBe $1M for misleading claims; 800+ overlay users still sued in 2023-24. Adrian Roselli's tracking: https://adrianroselli.com/2020/06/accessibe-will-get-you-sued.html ; FTC: https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/03/ftc-orders-ai-accessibility-startup-accessibe-to-pay-1m-for-misleading-advertising

4.1.2.platform: Contact/checkout forms in Gravity Forms, Wix Forms, Shopify checkout, HubSpot forms
4.1.2.name: Required state and errors conveyed by color/asterisk only, not programmatically
4.1.2.description: Required fields are marked with a red asterisk or red border (color/symbol only) with no required/aria-required and no legend explaining the asterisk. On submit, errors are shown as red text near fields but not associated via aria-describedby and the field gets no aria-invalid, so screen readers never learn the field is required, that it errored, or what the message says.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Invalid email
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare visible label may satisfy the form-label check, but tools cannot tell that requiredness/error is conveyed by COLOR alone (1.4.1), cannot verify an error message is the CORRECT suggestion (3.3.3), and cannot confirm the on-submit error text is programmatically tied to the field — these need a human to submit the form and inspect the associations and meaning.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million 2026: missing form labels on 51% of pages (top error): https://webaim.org/projects/million/ ; required-field color-only guidance: https://www.deque.com/blog/aria-requiredtrue-wcag-2-compliance-practice/

4.1.2.platform: Bootstrap/template tabs, accordions, and custom dropdowns in CMS themes
4.1.2.name: Custom widget role present but state/keyboard support missing
4.1.2.description: A theme implements tabs/accordions/menus with role=tab/button and ARIA, satisfying role checks, but the dynamic VALUE/STATE is wrong or static: aria-expanded never toggles, aria-selected is hard-coded, the panel relationship (aria-controls) is broken, and arrow-key navigation is absent. ARIA presence makes the page LOOK accessible while behaving inaccessibly.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<button aria-expanded="false" class="accordion">Shipping</button>
<!-- clicking opens the panel visually but aria-expanded stays "false"; no arrow-key support -->
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static scans confirm the ATTRIBUTES exist and are valid; they cannot verify the attribute VALUE tracks the live UI state (aria-expanded staying false after opening) or that keyboard interaction patterns work — these are dynamic, requiring activation and re-inspection. This is precisely why WebAIM finds MORE detected errors on ARIA-heavy pages.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million: pages WITH ARIA average ~34-69% MORE detected errors than pages without — broken/incomplete ARIA is a leading cause: https://webaim.org/projects/million/2024 ; 2026 confirms the pattern: https://webaim.org/projects/million/

4.1.2.platform: Cookie-consent banners, newsletter modals, promo pop-ups (OneTrust, Privy, Mailchimp, Wix popups)
4.1.2.name: Modal/pop-up keyboard trap or focus-not-managed
4.1.2.description: A modal or interstitial appears but focus is not moved into it, focus is not trapped within it (so keyboard users tab to the obscured page behind), or — the inverse failure — focus IS trapped with no keyboard-reachable close, stranding the user. The page behind also remains in the tab order under the overlay.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Focus behavior is dynamic and only observable by actually tabbing through after the modal opens. A static scan sees a div with some content; it cannot detect that focus was never moved in, that the user can tab behind the overlay, or that there is no keyboard escape (2.1.2). Requires manual keyboard testing.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: The Murphy v. Eyebobs overlay case specifically cited a promo pop-up and a modal dialog that were not keyboard/screen-reader accessible: https://www.accessibility.works/blog/avoid-accessibility-overlay-tools-toolbar-plugins/ ; modal focus-trap failures are a top serial-plaintiff demand-letter item.

4.1.2.platform: Hand-coded / framework icon buttons with aria-label overriding visible text (e.g. Bootstrap/Tailwind 'Submit' button decorated with aria-label="Send form now")
4.1.2.name: aria-label contradicts visible button text (Label in Name break)
4.1.2.description: A control has visible text but aria-label replaces it with different wording, so the accessible name no longer contains the visible label. Speech-input users cannot activate it by speaking the visible word, and screen-reader users hear different text than sighted users see. The classic W3C example is a 'Go' button whose aria-label is 'Find in this site'.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Cart (3)
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe/Lighthouse see a non-empty accessible name and a button with a role, so they pass it. They do not (reliably) compare the visible text node against the computed accessible name to detect that the visible label is absent from the name; deciding whether the visible word is 'contained' requires reading both strings and judging semantic equivalence.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: W3C WCAG failure F96 (accessible name not containing visible label text) uses the 'Go' button with aria-label 'Find in this site'; documented by Adrian Roselli and Ashlee Boyer ('Don't Overwrite Visual Labels With aria-label'). https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/failures/F96

4.1.2.platform: Custom widgets / CMS templates where aria-labelledby points to an element that was deleted, never rendered, or is empty (e.g. Drupal book nav, modal dialogs)
4.1.2.name: aria-labelledby referencing a broken / empty IDREF
4.1.2.description: aria-labelledby names an id that does not exist in the DOM, has a typo or case mismatch, or resolves to an element whose text content is empty. Per the accname spec a broken or empty reference yields an empty accessible name, so the control or landmark is unnamed even though the author 'added a label'.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one is largely catchable: axe flags aria-labelledby IDREFs that do not resolve, and an empty resulting name. It is included for completeness. The residual human case is when the IDREF resolves to a node that is present but contextually wrong (points to the right id but the wrong text), which a linter cannot judge.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Drupal book module broke aria-labelledby IDREFs in navigation (issue 3119008); SiteLint/axe rule 'aria-labelledby must reference an existing element'. https://www.drupal.org/project/book/issues/3119008

4.1.2.platform: Marketing-site / CMS clickable cards and tiles built as div/span with onclick (Webflow interactions, custom hero tiles, jQuery .click handlers)
4.1.2.name: div/span with click handler as a fake button (no role, no keyboard)
4.1.2.description: An interactive control is a bare div or span with a JS click handler, no role, no tabindex, and only an onclick (no keydown). Keyboard users cannot reach or activate it, and screen readers announce nothing meaningful. This is the canonical W3C F59 failure.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Pricing

See plans
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Partially auto-detectable (axe 'interactive controls must be operable' / clickable element flags exist), but tools frequently miss it when the handler is attached via addEventListener at runtime rather than an inline onclick attribute, or delegated from a parent. Confirming it is genuinely interactive (vs. a decorative animated div) often needs a human to click/Tab and observe.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: W3C failure F59 (script makes div/span a UI control without a role); Deque 'Building Accessible Buttons with ARIA'. https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/F59.html

4.1.2.platform: Icon-only controls (font-icon or SVG) labelled only via the HTML title attribute (e.g. linked social icons, table action icons)
4.1.2.name: title attribute as the sole accessible name
4.1.2.description: A linked icon or icon button has no text and no aria-label; its only name is a title attribute. title is exposed inconsistently across screen readers (JAWS/NVDA/VoiceOver differ, and it is suppressed when an img alt is present), so the control is effectively unnamed for many users and provides only a flaky mouse-hover tooltip with no keyboard equivalent.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Per the accname algorithm title IS a valid (last-resort) name source, so axe computes a non-empty accessible name and passes the element. Whether the title is actually announced (and is adequate) depends on the screen reader and on whether better naming was intended; judging the real-world failure needs a human testing with AT.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: 24a11y 'Trials and Tribulations of the Title Attribute'; Silktide 'I thought title text improved accessibility. I was wrong.'; W3C issue 867 on title as sole accName. https://www.24a11y.com/2017/the-trials-and-tribulations-of-the-title-attribute/

4.1.2.platform: Hamburger menus and disclosure widgets from page builders / themes (YOOtheme mobile nav, custom accordions) where aria-expanded is static
4.1.2.name: aria-expanded set once and never toggled
4.1.2.description: A toggle button carries aria-expanded but the value is hardcoded (or missing) and never updated by the open/close JS, so it announces 'collapsed' even when the menu/panel is open (or vice versa). Screen-reader users get the wrong state and cannot tell whether activating it will reveal or hide content.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<button class="nav-toggle" aria-expanded="false">Menu</button>
<!-- panel opens visually; attribute stays "false" -->
<nav class="is-open">...</nav>
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A static snapshot has a valid aria-expanded value, so a single-state scan passes. Detecting the stale value requires interacting (open the menu) and comparing the visual/DOM open-state against the attribute over time — a dynamic, stateful check most automated scans do not perform.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: YOOtheme support thread 'WCAG 2.1 - Missing aria-expanded on mobile hamburger menu'; David MacDonald 'How to toggle aria-expanded'. https://yootheme.com/support/question/170328

4.1.2.platform: Custom toggle switches / checkboxes (role="switch" or role="checkbox" from design-system components, e.g. settings toggles) whose aria-checked is not synced
4.1.2.name: aria-checked / aria-selected / aria-pressed never updated to match visual state
4.1.2.description: A custom switch, checkbox, tab, or toggle button shows its state visually (color, knob position) but the aria-checked / aria-selected / aria-pressed attribute is never flipped in JS, so AT always reports the same state. The visual model and the exposed state diverge.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Notifications
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Statically, the required state attribute is present and valid, so structural ARIA rules pass. The failure is the mismatch between rendered visual state and the attribute, which needs a human to toggle the control and confirm what AT announces vs. what the UI shows.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Adrian Roselli 'Switch Role Support'; designsystemproblems.com toggle-switch accessibility guide on keeping aria-checked in sync. https://adrianroselli.com/2021/10/switch-role-support.html

4.1.2.platform: Modal dialogs, off-canvas drawers, and carousels (Bootstrap modal backdrops, slick/swiper slides, third-party overlay libs) that set aria-hidden on containers holding focusable elements
4.1.2.name: aria-hidden="true" on (or wrapping) focusable elements
4.1.2.description: A container is hidden from AT with aria-hidden="true" but still contains tabbable controls (links, buttons, inputs) that were not made inert / tabindex=-1. Keyboard users can Tab into a control the screen reader refuses to announce — 'focus goes nowhere' — producing a phantom/ghost focus and broken navigation. Common on inactive carousel slides and behind-modal page content.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Buy now
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Mostly auto-detectable (axe rule 'aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable elements'). Included for completeness. Tools can miss it when focusability comes from runtime-added tabindex, or when the aria-hidden is toggled on only in a state (modal open) the scanner never enters; reaching that state is a human/dynamic step.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: GetWCAG 4.1.2 fix guide 'avoid focusable elements inside aria-hidden containers'; ACT rules issue 643; UW accessibility 'aria-hidden elements'. https://getwcag.com/en/accessibility-guide/aria-hidden-focus

4.1.2.platform: Layout/data tables and styled lists where authors apply role="presentation"/role="none" to strip default styling (theme CSS resets, email-style layout tables, framework grid wrappers)
4.1.2.name: role="presentation"/"none" on content that conveys structure (semantics stripped)
4.1.2.description: role=presentation or role=none is placed on a genuine data table, list, or heading to defeat browser styling, which removes its semantics. Screen-reader users lose row/column relationships, list item counts, or heading navigation — the W3C F92 failure. Even worse when applied to a focusable/interactive element, which keeps focus but loses its announced role.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
PlanPrice
Pro$9
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe will not flag a layout table with role=presentation — that is the legitimate use. Distinguishing a real DATA table (headers convey relationships, so presentation is wrong) from a true layout table requires reading the content and judging whether the structure is meaningful; that is a semantic call no linter makes reliably.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: W3C failure F92 (role presentation on content that conveys semantics); PowerMapper 'Data table hidden by role=presentation'. https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/F92.html

4.1.2.platform: Form fields in CMS form builders and templates (WordPress/Webflow forms, custom inputs) where the placeholder is the only label
4.1.2.name: placeholder used as the only label / instruction
4.1.2.description: An input has no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — only a placeholder. The placeholder is low-contrast, vanishes on focus/typing (so users lose the field's name mid-entry), is not consistently treated as an accessible name by all AT, and offers no persistent instruction. Often paired with required-field and format hints living only in the placeholder.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<input type="email" placeholder="Email address">
<input type="text" placeholder="MM/DD/YYYY">
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Browsers may expose placeholder as a fallback accessible name, so some scanners report a name present and pass it (axe does warn in some configs, but inconsistently across the suite). The disappearing-on-input UX failure and the lost-instruction problem are behavioral/visual and need human judgment; the contrast of placeholder text is also an easily-missed visual check.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: MDN/WebAIM and reform.app 'Common ARIA Mistakes in Forms' document placeholder-as-label as a top form anti-pattern. https://www.reform.app/blog/common-aria-mistakes-in-forms-and-fixes

4.1.2.platform: Redundant/conflicting roles from copy-pasted ARIA snippets and component libraries (role on native elements, e.g. role="button" on <button>, role="link" on <a>, role="list" stripping then re-adding)
4.1.2.name: redundant or wrong explicit role on a native element
4.1.2.description: ARIA is layered onto an element that already had the right native semantics, or onto the wrong element. Redundant role="button" on <button> is merely noise, but role="menuitem" on a plain link, role="text" on a heading, or aria-label on a non-interactive <div> that suppresses children create incorrect or missing semantics. 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.'
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Home

Features

  • ...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Many redundant-role cases are technically valid ARIA (role allowed on the element), so axe passes them; only a subset (abstract roles, role conflicts) is flagged. Deciding that role="button" on a link is semantically WRONG (it navigates, so it should be a link) requires understanding the element's actual behavior — a human semantic judgment.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: W3C 'Using ARIA' rule 1 / 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA'; BarrierBreak 'Top 5 ARIA Implementation Errors'. https://www.barrierbreak.com/top-5-aria-implementation-errors/

4.1.2.platform: Color-only state and variant controls from e-commerce and design systems (product color swatches, 'selected' tab/chip indicated only by color, required-field asterisks colored red only)
4.1.2.name: ARIA state/selection conveyed by color only, not exposed to AT
4.1.2.description: The selected swatch, active filter chip, current tab, or required field is distinguished purely by a color change with no aria-selected/aria-current/aria-pressed and no text/icon. Sighted users see the active variant; AT and colorblind users get no programmatic or non-color indication of which option is chosen.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<button class="swatch swatch--selected" style="background:#c00"></button>
<button class="swatch" style="background:#00c"></button>
<!-- 'selected' is only a border color; no aria-pressed/label -->
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each swatch is a valid button; nothing in the markup is malformed. Detecting that 'selected' is signalled only by color, and that no equivalent state is exposed, requires visually comparing states and reasoning that color is the sole differentiator — a combined visual + semantic judgment automated scanners cannot make. The swatches also typically have no accessible name (the color name), another human-named gap.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color; e-commerce color-swatch audits (Deque/WebAIM) repeatedly flag color-only selection and unnamed swatches on Shopify/Magento product pages.

4.1.2.platform: Required fields and inline validation in form builders / SPA forms where required and error state are visual-only (red border, red asterisk) without aria-required / aria-invalid / aria-describedby
4.1.2.name: form error and required state not programmatically associated
4.1.2.description: A field is marked required with a red asterisk and, on submit, an error appears as red text below it — but the input has no aria-required, no aria-invalid="true", and the error message is not tied via aria-describedby. Screen-reader users do not learn the field is required, that it errored, or what the suggested fix is.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Enter a valid email
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error markup is valid HTML and the field has a label, so structural scans pass. The failure is the missing programmatic ASSOCIATION between input, its required/invalid state, and the message text — which only surfaces by submitting the form (a dynamic step) and judging whether the announced output conveys the error and a suggestion; scanners do not trigger validation or evaluate message quality.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WCAG 3.3.1/3.3.3 and reform.app 'Common ARIA Mistakes in Forms'; red-asterisk-only required and unassociated inline errors are among the most common audited form failures. https://www.reform.app/blog/common-aria-mistakes-in-forms-and-fixes

4.1.2.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce / Magento product-variant color swatches
4.1.2.name: Color-only swatch with no text label or out-of-stock cue
4.1.2.description: Selectable variant swatches are rendered as colored squares/circles whose only differentiator is the fill color, with no accessible name for the color and no non-color indication of state. "Out of stock" or "unavailable" variants are signaled purely by graying-out, and the selected swatch is shown only by a subtle color/border change. Color-blind and screen-reader users cannot tell red from green, which swatch is chosen, or which are unavailable.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: An empty <button> with no name may trip a 4.1.2 rule, but the use-of-color failure (state and meaning conveyed only by hue, no text/icon equivalent) is invisible to automation — tools cannot determine that color is the sole carrier of "selected"/"out of stock" or that two swatches are only distinguishable by hue. That is a visual-semantic call.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Shopify/EAA swatch guidance and Bricks/Salesforce CC audits flag color-only swatches and out-of-stock graying as a11y problems requiring text labels. https://craftshift.com/shopify-european-accessibility-act-swatches/ and https://forum.bricksbuilder.io/t/accessibility-issue-with-color-variation-swatches-edited-new-issue/38992

4.1.2.platform: Theme components using icon fonts / inline SVG (Font Awesome, Bootstrap icons, Shopify Dawn header)
4.1.2.name: Icon-only button/link with no accessible name
4.1.2.description: A hamburger, search magnifier, close X, cart, or social-share control is rendered as a button/anchor whose only content is an <i> icon-font glyph or a decorative <svg> with no aria-label, no visually hidden text, and no title. Screen readers announce a bare "button" or "link" with no indication of what it does; voice-control users have nothing to target.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one is largely catchable: axe/Lighthouse flag buttons and links with no accessible name. (Edge cases where an icon font ligature renders visible text the AT can read, or where a name exists but is wrong, still need human review, but the bare unnamed-control case is a reliable linter hit.)
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Icon-only controls are the canonical 4.1.2 "button with no accessible name" failure; Font Awesome's own docs and Shopify Dawn audits call it out. https://docs.fontawesome.com/web/dig-deeper/accessibility and https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

4.1.2.platform: Page-builder custom widgets (Elementor/WPBakery div "buttons", custom controls with aria-label)
4.1.2.name: div role=button whose accessible name contradicts its visible label
4.1.2.description: A builder renders an interactive control as a <div>/<span> with role="button" (or no role at all) and an aria-label that was authored separately from the visible text — so the on-screen label says "Submit" while the accessible name is "Send form", or the visible text is "Get Quote" but aria-label is "button". Voice-control users saying the visible word can't activate it, and screen-reader users hear something different from what's shown; when role is missing entirely, it isn't even reachable by keyboard.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Submit
Get Quote
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: When an aria-label is present the control HAS an accessible name, so 4.1.2 "has a name" passes; comparing that name against the visible rendered text to detect a mismatch requires OCR/text extraction of the visible label and a semantic equality judgment that automation doesn't make reliably. (The pure missing-role/not-focusable variant is more linter-catchable.)
4.1.2.realWorldNote: div role=button with aria-label diverging from visible text is the canonical accessible-name-mismatch failure (also a 2.5.3 issue). https://www.makethingsaccessible.com/guides/say-what-you-see-wcag-2-5-3-label-in-name-level-a/ and https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/failures/F96.html

4.1.3.platform: Toast / snackbar (MUI Snackbar misused, hand-rolled notifications, Toastify)
4.1.3.name: Toast rendered into a plain div, not a live region
4.1.3.description: A 'Saved!' or 'Error: try again' toast is injected into a positioned <div> with no role="status"/role="alert" and no aria-live. The message animates in visually but is never announced, so screen reader users never learn the action succeeded or failed.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The toast container is valid HTML with valid contrast and valid markup — there is nothing structurally wrong for a linter to flag. Whether the absence of aria-live constitutes a violation depends on the div being a dynamically-injected status message, which a static scan of the final DOM cannot infer; you must observe that new content appeared without an announcement, a runtime + semantic judgment.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Adrian Roselli's 'Defining Toast Messages' and the elastic/eui issue #715 'Toast Messages Should Be Read by the Screen Reader on Display' document toasts shipping without live regions in production component libraries. https://adrianroselli.com/2020/01/defining-toast-messages.html and https://github.com/elastic/eui/issues/715

4.1.3.platform: Combobox / autocomplete (typeahead search, React-Select clones, hand-rolled)
4.1.3.name: Autocomplete results not announced; missing aria-expanded/activedescendant
4.1.3.description: A search input shows a dropdown of suggestions visually, but the input lacks role="combobox", aria-expanded never flips to true when the list opens, and aria-activedescendant is not set as the user arrows through results. Screen reader users get no announcement that suggestions appeared, how many there are, or which one is highlighted.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
• apple
  • apricot
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The input is a valid text field and the list is a valid <ul> — both pass static checks individually. The relationship (input controls a popup list whose active option must be announced) and the missing live/activedescendant feedback only manifest while typing and arrowing, so DOM-snapshot tools cannot see the broken announcement loop.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: The a11ysupport.io APG combobox test and Pope Tech's combobox guide document that aria-expanded must toggle and aria-activedescendant must track the highlighted option, and that omitting them is the dominant real-world combobox failure. https://a11ysupport.io/tests/apg__aria-1-2-combobox-with-list-autocomplete-example

4.1.3.platform: Single-page app (React Router, Vue Router, Angular) route transitions
4.1.3.name: <title> and focus never update on client-side route change
4.1.3.description: Navigating between SPA 'pages' swaps the DOM without a reload, but document.title is left at the template default ('My App') for every route, focus stays on the clicked link or the top of the old view, and no live region announces the new page. Screen reader users have no idea they navigated or where they are; the page title — a primary orientation cue — is identical or stale across routes.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
<title>My App</title>
<!-- user clicks 'Checkout'; URL becomes /checkout; main content swaps -->
<!-- <title> still 'My App'; focus still on the clicked nav link; no aria-live announcement -->
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-snapshot scan sees one <title> that is present and non-empty, so 2.4.2 passes. The defect is that the title is the SAME (or unchanged) across multiple distinct views — only visible by navigating between routes and comparing, plus judging that the title no longer describes the content. Automated tools audit one URL state, not transitions.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Hidde de Vries, Kitty Giraudel, and Deque all document SPA route changes leaving document.title stale and focus unmanaged as a flagship screen-reader failure of frameworks. https://hidde.blog/accessible-page-titles-in-a-single-page-app/ and https://www.deque.com/blog/accessibility-tips-in-single-page-applications/

4.1.3.name: Critical confirm dialog uses role=dialog (or none) so it is not announced
4.1.3.description: A 'Delete account — are you sure?' modal is built with role="dialog" (or plain divs) rather than role="alertdialog", and focus is not moved into it. The urgent message is not announced as an alert, focus stays behind it, and a screen reader user may confirm a destructive action without ever hearing the warning.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Delete your account? This cannot be undone.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=dialog is valid ARIA, so no rule fails. Whether the dialog SHOULD be an alertdialog (because it carries an urgent, action-blocking message) is a semantic/contextual judgment about the content's importance; whether focus moves into it and the alert is announced are runtime behaviors. No static linter weighs the urgency of a message.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: APG distinguishes alertdialog (interrupts with an important message requiring a response) from dialog; MDN dialog-role docs note focus must move into the dialog — both are commonly skipped on confirm/destructive modals. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/dialog_role

4.1.3.platform: Spinbutton / number stepper (quantity +/- controls in carts)
4.1.3.name: Stepper +/- buttons with icon-only names and no spinbutton value semantics
4.1.3.description: A quantity stepper has '+' and '−' buttons (often unlabeled icon glyphs) around a value, but the value display is a plain <span> with no role="spinbutton"/aria-valuenow, and the increment/decrement buttons have no accessible name (just a glyph) or a name that does not say what they change. Screen reader users hear 'button button' and an unchanging value when they press them.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: 1
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: If the buttons contain a glyph character (−/+) axe may consider them to have text and pass discernible-text; the '−' may even be read as 'minus' or skipped. Judging that the name does not convey 'decrease quantity' is semantic, and the value <span> not exposing changes (no spinbutton role / live update) is a runtime announcement gap a snapshot scan cannot detect.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: The APG spinbutton pattern requires role=spinbutton with aria-valuenow/min/max and accessible names on the controls; e-commerce quantity steppers commonly ship as glyph-only buttons around a non-semantic value span, a frequent audit finding. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/

4.1.3.platform: React/Vue/Angular SPAs built on Next.js, Gatsby, Shopify Hydrogen, headless storefronts
4.1.3.name: SPA <title> and focus never update on client-side route change
4.1.3.description: Navigating between client-rendered views swaps the main content but never updates document.title and never moves focus, so the page title is frozen at the initial route ('Home') and the screen reader is left on a now-detached element. The user has no confirmation a navigation happened or where they landed.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
<!-- title stuck on first load across every route -->
<title>Acme Store - Home</title>
<!-- /products, /cart, /checkout all render under this same title; no focus move, no live-region announce -->
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-snapshot scan sees a valid, non-empty <title> and passes 2.4.2. The failure is DYNAMIC and BEHAVIORAL — it only manifests across a route transition, which axe/Lighthouse (point-in-time DOM scans) never exercise. Catching it requires interacting (clicking a nav link) and observing that title/focus did not change.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Documented SPA failure mode; Kitty Giraudel and Deque both cover the fix (update title + manage focus/live region on route change): https://kittygiraudel.com/2020/01/15/accessible-title-in-a-single-page-react-application/ , https://www.deque.com/blog/accessibility-tips-in-single-page-applications/

4.1.3.platform: MUI Snackbar, react-hot-toast, Bootstrap toasts, Shopify/WordPress 'added to cart' confirmations
4.1.3.name: Toast / status confirmation not in a live region
4.1.3.description: A success/error toast or 'Added to cart' / 'Form submitted' confirmation appears visually but is injected into a plain <div> with no role=status/alert and no aria-live, so screen readers announce nothing. The toast then auto-dismisses, so the information is gone before a non-visual user could ever discover it.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Item added to your cart
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The toast container often does not exist in the DOM at scan time (injected on an action) and, when present, a missing aria-live is not flagged because a div with text is perfectly valid HTML. Determining that THIS particular transient message needed to be announced is a semantic judgment about what the content means to the user, not a structural rule.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: MUI Snackbar accessibility gaps are tracked upstream (focus/ESC/announce issues): https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/22354 . Sara Soueidan on live-region notification pitfalls: https://www.sarasoueidan.com/blog/accessible-notifications-with-aria-live-regions-part-1/

4.1.3.platform: WordPress slider plugins (Slider Revolution, Smart Slider), Elementor/Divi carousels, Wix Pro Gallery
4.1.3.name: Auto-rotating carousel, keyboard-inaccessible, no pause
4.1.3.description: A hero carousel auto-advances on a timer with no pause/stop control, prev/next arrows are non-focusable divs, and slide changes are not announced. Keyboard users cannot reach controls; the moving content steals reading position; offscreen slides may still be in the tab order as hidden focusable links.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Shop the sale
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Auto-rotation timing and the absence of a pause control are temporal/behavioral and not in the static DOM signature. Tools may catch a div with onclick lacking a role, but cannot verify keyboard reachability of the rotation, that focus is trapped/lost between slides, or that offscreen slides leak into the tab order — all need manual keyboard testing.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: WCAG-ART and the A11Y Collective document carousel pause/keyboard/announce failures as classic manual-test items: https://www.a11y-collective.com/blog/accessible-carousel/ ; WP slider accessibility caveats: https://www.abrightclearweb.com/accessible-slider-wordpress/

4.1.3.platform: accessiBe / UserWay / AudioEye overlay widgets injected over any CMS
4.1.3.name: Overlay-injected accessible names that mismatch the visible control
4.1.3.description: An automated accessibility-overlay 'fixes' controls by injecting aria-labels guessed from nearby text, icons, or filenames. The injected name frequently does not match the control's visible label or function (a 'Search' field labeled 'button', a close 'X' labeled 'menu'), so the accessible name and visible label diverge — and the widget can also trap screen-reader focus after its own dialog closes.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
<!-- overlay rewrites this -->
<button aria-label="link 2">Contact Us</button>
<input type="search" aria-label="submit" placeholder="Search...">
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Both the overlay's injected name and the visible label are syntactically valid, so a linter sees an accessible name present and passes. Detecting that the programmatic NAME contradicts the VISIBLE label (and that voice-control users can no longer say the label) requires comparing rendered text against the computed name — a human semantic comparison. Tools that scan post-overlay DOM are actively fooled.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: FTC fined accessiBe $1M for misleading claims; 800+ overlay users still sued in 2023-24. Adrian Roselli's tracking: https://adrianroselli.com/2020/06/accessibe-will-get-you-sued.html ; FTC: https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/03/ftc-orders-ai-accessibility-startup-accessibe-to-pay-1m-for-misleading-advertising

4.1.3.platform: Bootstrap/template tabs, accordions, and custom dropdowns in CMS themes
4.1.3.name: Custom widget role present but state/keyboard support missing
4.1.3.description: A theme implements tabs/accordions/menus with role=tab/button and ARIA, satisfying role checks, but the dynamic VALUE/STATE is wrong or static: aria-expanded never toggles, aria-selected is hard-coded, the panel relationship (aria-controls) is broken, and arrow-key navigation is absent. ARIA presence makes the page LOOK accessible while behaving inaccessibly.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
<button aria-expanded="false" class="accordion">Shipping</button>
<!-- clicking opens the panel visually but aria-expanded stays "false"; no arrow-key support -->
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static scans confirm the ATTRIBUTES exist and are valid; they cannot verify the attribute VALUE tracks the live UI state (aria-expanded staying false after opening) or that keyboard interaction patterns work — these are dynamic, requiring activation and re-inspection. This is precisely why WebAIM finds MORE detected errors on ARIA-heavy pages.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million: pages WITH ARIA average ~34-69% MORE detected errors than pages without — broken/incomplete ARIA is a leading cause: https://webaim.org/projects/million/2024 ; 2026 confirms the pattern: https://webaim.org/projects/million/

4.1.3.platform: Toast / snackbar notifications and async status from SPA component libraries (custom toasts, some MUI/Chakra usages) rendered without a live region
4.1.3.name: toast / status message not in a live region (silent announcement)
4.1.3.description: A success/error toast or 'Saved' confirmation is injected into the DOM with no role="status"/role="alert" and no aria-live, so screen-reader users never hear it. Conversely, some use role="alert"/assertive for low-priority messages and interrupt/clobber the user. The visual feedback has no programmatic announcement.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Your changes were saved
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: There is no markup defect to flag — the toast div is perfectly valid HTML. Knowing it SHOULD have been a status message (it conveys a status change) and that it currently announces nothing requires understanding the message's purpose and testing the dynamic update with AT; automated scanners do not model 'this content appeared and should have been announced'.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Sara Soueidan 'Accessible notifications with ARIA Live Regions'; TPGI live-region support; htmhell ARIA Live Regions — all note injected toasts commonly go un-announced. https://www.sarasoueidan.com/blog/accessible-notifications-with-aria-live-regions-part-1/

4.1.3.platform: Single-page apps (React Router / Vue Router / Angular routing in SPA themes and dashboards) where document.title is not updated on route change
4.1.3.name: SPA <title> never updates on client-side route change
4.1.3.description: Navigating between client-side routes swaps the view but leaves <title> at the initial app shell value (e.g. 'My App'). Screen-reader users get no title announcement on 'navigation', browser tabs/history/bookmarks all read the same generic title, and there is no programmatic signal that the page changed.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page scan finds a valid, non-empty <title>, so 2.4.2 passes. The defect only manifests across route transitions — the scanner would have to drive the SPA, change routes, and compare titles. Judging whether each route's title is unique and descriptive is also a contextual call.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Widely documented SPA a11y gap (gov.uk / Marcy Sutton / TPGI guidance on managing focus and document.title on route change in React/Vue/Angular SPAs).

4.1.3.platform: Material UI Snackbar / generic React toast libraries
4.1.3.name: Toast/snackbar fired outside a live region
4.1.3.description: A transient toast ("Item added to cart", "Saved", "Error: try again") is injected into the DOM as a styled <div> with no role="status"/role="alert" and not inside an aria-live region. Sighted users see it appear and fade; screen-reader users get no announcement at all, so success/error feedback is silently lost. Often compounded by auto-dismiss before any AT could reach it.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The toast exists only momentarily and contains valid markup; static scanners audit a snapshot of the DOM and have no concept of "this content appeared dynamically and was not announced." Detecting it requires observing the runtime mutation and judging that it is a status message that needed a live region.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Documented as a recurring toast failure; MUI Snackbar focus/announcement issues are tracked upstream. https://www.sarasoueidan.com/blog/accessible-notifications-with-aria-live-regions-part-1/ and https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/22354
